title: Duplicate orders, sandbox ledger

headlines.label: Scenarios that end with more than one PayPal order or authorization (100 duplicate-prone scenarios, sandbox ledger)
headlines.note: Sandbox ledger: the real gate, request id, order body and vault authorization sent to the PayPal sandbox; duplicates counted from PayPal's own order and authorization records. PayPal holds 100 orders for 100 intended purchases. 140 create requests reached PayPal; for 40 of them PayPal answered a repeated PayPal-Request-Id with the order it already had.

headlines.label: Lost PayPal answer (dropped after PayPal answered), then a resend or a new readback: scenarios with a second PayPal order (sandbox ledger)
headlines.baseline: before the fix, same id: 10 of 20
headlines.note: 60 answers dropped at the network edge; PayPal had created the first order in 20 of 20 (read back from PayPal). Resend on the same confirmation: 0 of 10; new readback within minutes: 0 of 10.

headlines.label: Same lost-answer scenarios before the fix (hold released, buyer told nothing was charged), sandbox ledger
headlines.baseline: random request id per attempt: 20 of 20
headlines.note: Before fix, kept for comparison; second orders here are real PayPal sandbox orders (authorized, then voided). Local simulation across all 100: 10 of 100, random id 20 of 100.

headlines.label: Lost PayPal answer, buyer buys the same item again after the 10-minute duplicate window: second PayPal order (sandbox ledger)
headlines.note: Separate probe, not in the 100. The ten-minute gap is on the virtual clock; PayPal calls are made in order, a few seconds apart.

headlines.label: Buyer comes back after a lost PayPal answer, then would buy again: second PayPal order (sandbox ledger)
headlines.note: Reconciliation re-sent the original create with the original PayPal-Request-Id; PayPal returned the order it had created from the dropped request in 10 of 10.

headlines.label: PayPal orders in this suite whose amount, payee or quantity differ from the confirmed readback (sandbox ledger)
Sandbox authorizations voided at the end of their scenario
headlines.note: Every authorization the run created, including those from dropped answers, is voided so the sandbox buyer is never charged.

limitations: Sandbox ledger: the real gate, request id, order body and vault authorization sent to the PayPal sandbox; duplicates counted from PayPal's own order and authorization records. One run against the sandbox; PayPal's sandbox may behave differently from production, and its request-id retention was only exercised over minutes, not hours.

Only the PayPal side is real. The buyer side runs on the local run's virtual clock (scripted timings, last-writer-wins session state, two independent tabs), and the orders table and Postgres budget holds of payForReadback are replaced by local orders and the gate's InMemoryLedger, read the way gate-ports.ts reads the database. The pay step's PayPal half is the app's own code (orderInputFromCart, createVaultOrder, completeOrder).

A lost answer is simulated at the network edge only: PayPal received every create and answered; the answer was dropped before the HTTP client saw it, and the client retried with the same PayPal-Request-Id. A request that never reached PayPal was not tested.

The OUTCOME_UNKNOWN block follows payments.ts exactly (an unsettled order for the same item on another readback); the local simulation also blocks a resend on the same readback. Either way, a resend on the same readback carries the same PayPal-Request-Id.
Intent AUTHORIZE throughout (the readback says PayPal holds the money until the item checks out); nothing is captured and every authorization is voided. The local run uses CAPTURE.

Only the current policy with the bound request id runs on all 100 scenarios and the after-window probe; the before-fix baseline runs on the 20 lost-answer scenarios only. The hold_kept policy is local only.
Key 2 is a stub that agrees exactly when key 1 does; the real classifier needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Transaction Search cross-check (secondary): 0 of 190 authorization ids listed when read at the end of the run; 0 transactions in the window. It can lag by hours, so it is not used for any count.

details.label: Sandbox ledger: the real gate, request id, order body and vault authorization sent to the PayPal sandbox; duplicates counted from PayPal's own order and authorization records
details.duplicateDefinition: A scenario (one intended purchase) for which PayPal holds more than one order, or more than one authorization, among the orders its create requests produced. Order ids come from PayPal's answers at the network edge (dropped answers included); each order and authorization is then read with GET.
details.requestId: paypalRequestId('order', cart.hash, readback.id), computed by runGate; sent by createVaultOrder
details.pacing: At most 2 requests a second at the network edge; on 429 the edge waits (Retry-After or exponential) and halves its rate.

transactionSearch.note: Secondary check only. PayPal says transactions can take up to three hours to appear in Transaction Search, so it is read once at the end of the run and a shortfall is expected lag, not a missing payment. The primary count is from Orders v2 and Payments v2 GETs.
